### Retained fanout-project inspection — [redacted] / execution_integrity

The existing Ledger stores a project's complete plan and task/result evidence, but consumers can only query individual parts and separate queued/completed sets. An operator reopening a recorded project needs one coherent read-only view before deciding whether to dispatch or reconcile it.

Source baseline: `d65bde9c59b1d2593a80f6d838c0a40bf6768013`, complete tree `d5e5ad4e316be0b20a50151f8549ac490d3d99de`. All12 existing files are captured; current project issue/PR reads found no competing scope and there is no AGENTS file. An actual eight-part in-memory baseline has five dependency-ready parts, four queued parts, and only `notes` in their intersection. Unknown, failed, running and unfinished dependencies are visible in the existing state; 13 event rows remain unchanged. This is an absent inspection workflow, not a claim of incorrect dispatch.

`[redacted]/execution_integrity` owns the bounded contribution: one additive snapshot SELECT in `fanout_engine/ledger.py`, new `fanout_engine/inspection.py`, additive public export in `fanout_engine/__init__.py`, new `examples/inspect_plan.py`, focused `tests/test_inspection.py`, and a README section, plus unique source/qualification evidence. The public `inspect_project(ledger, project_id)` consumes the already-recorded plan, preserving native task/route/artifact/evidence references and original ordering. It reports direct unfinished dependencies, counts and the queued/dependency-ready intersection from one coherent read.

Unknown project, missing parts and malformed/inconsistent stored data receive explicit read errors without mutation. Valid native constructor representations must remain valid, including preserved tag/dependency order; parsing must not silently normalize an existing recorded identity. Results are detached JSON-compatible values. Existing schema, transitions, plan/dispatcher/router, retries and reconciliation remain unchanged. No new scheduler, service, store, provider call or live project mutation is introduced.

Root independently receives and serializes source publication through the existing repository process and Python3.10/3.11/3.12 CI. Initial discovery receipt SHA256 `557201a05a56ae346d063e35113569bf447c420e77925f0497746afef75a0a45`; complete baseline manifest `db1a041094adb5178e59e66165b2b79ae9493009cb79fab09b9853e0f7eab483`. Local capacity limitations are separate from source behavior and will retain exact evidence.

The attempted project issue creation returned HTTP410 because Issues is disabled in `multi-agent-fanout-engine`; no issue was created and the setting will remain unchanged. This existing coordination thread is the source-scope record. Empty issue reads are not evidence of exhaustive ownership coverage; the current project PR and central source-claim searches are the applicable coordination evidence. The normal pull-request process remains the intended source receiving path.
